These data primitives represent a unified interface to working with our platform, whether it be structure prediction, binder design or inverse folding.

sections.heading: Protein
sections.prose: [`Protein`](#openprotein.molecules.Protein) is a fundamental primitive for working with proteins on the platform. These can be uploaded to our platform as a [`Query`](#openprotein.prompt.Query) to be used with models like [`ProteinMPNN`](#openprotein.models.ProteinMPNN) or [`ESMIF1`](#openprotein.models.ESMIF1) (e.g. for inverse-folding), as well as for ease of reuse.

sections.heading: Complex
sections.prose: [`Complex`](#openprotein.molecules.Complex) describes a molecular complex representation. These can be uploaded to our platform as a [`Query`](#openprotein.prompt.Query) to be used with models like [`RFdiffusion`](#openprotein.models.RFdiffusion), (e.g. for multi-chain binder design) as well as for easy reuse.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.prose: [`Structure`](#openprotein.molecules.Structure) describes a collection of [`Complex`](#Complex) instances. These are typically created when parsing structure files (e.g., CIF, PDB) that contain multiple models of the same molecular complex, such as NMR ensembles or computational predictions with multiple conformations.

sections.heading: Ligand
sections.prose: [`Ligand`](#openprotein.molecules.Ligand) represents a ligand that can be described either by ``smiles`` or ``ccd``. These are intended to be used as part of a [`Complex`](#Complex).

sections.heading: DNA
sections.prose: [`DNA`](#openprotein.molecules.DNA) represents a DNA chain. These are intended to be used as part of a [`Complex`](#Complex).

sections.heading: RNA
sections.prose: [`RNA`](#openprotein.molecules.RNA) represents a RNA chain. These are intended to be used as part of a [`Complex`](#Complex).

sections.heading: Template
sections.prose: [`Template`](#openprotein.molecules.Template) describes a template that can be used for constraining fold jobs.

sections.heading: Alignments and sampled prompts
sections.prose: An MSA can be downloaded, updated, or deleted. A prompt sampling future returns `list[list[str]]`, with the sequences in each replicate. `session.data.prompts.get(...)` retrieves a stored [`Prompt`](#openprotein.data.prompts.Prompt) handle; reloaded sampling jobs retain the compatibility [`Prompt`](/references/python-api/prompt#openprotein.prompt.Prompt) reader.

Use `session.models` as the primary interface for discovering and running models. `session.models.list_models()` lists models and `session.models.get_model(...)` retrieves one. Named accessors provide common families; `model.metadata`, `model.methods` and `model.params_schema(...)` expose metadata, available methods, and parameter schemas where supported. Inspect method descriptors for named outputs and their `default_output`.

Each specialized task future has a per-position result type T. `get()` and `wait()` return a list of T; `get_item()` and unit reads return T for a position; `stream()` returns an iterator of T.

| Future | Primary output | T per position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`EmbeddingFuture`](#openprotein.models.EmbeddingFuture) | `embeddings` | `numpy.ndarray` |
| [`LogitsFuture`](#openprotein.models.LogitsFuture) | `logits` | `numpy.ndarray` |
| [`AttentionFuture`](#openprotein.models.AttentionFuture) | `attn` | `numpy.ndarray` |
| [`LogLikelihoodFuture`](#openprotein.models.LogLikelihoodFuture) | `loglikelihood` | `float`, `list[float]`, or `numpy.ndarray` |
| [`SingleSiteScoreFuture`](#openprotein.models.SingleSiteScoreFuture) | `score` | `float`, `list[float]`, or `numpy.ndarray` |
| [`IndelScoreFuture`](#openprotein.models.IndelScoreFuture) | `score` | `float`, `list[float]`, or `numpy.ndarray` |
| [`SequenceGenerationFuture`](#openprotein.models.SequenceGenerationFuture) | `sequences` | `str` |
| [`PredictionFuture`](#openprotein.models.PredictionFuture) | `predictions` | `dict[str, Any]` |
| [`SingleSitePredictionFuture`](#openprotein.models.SingleSitePredictionFuture) | `predictions` | `dict[str, Any]` |
| [`StructureDesignFuture`](#openprotein.models.StructureDesignFuture) | `structures` | [`Complex`](#openprotein.molecules.Complex) |
| [`StructurePredictionFuture`](#openprotein.models.StructurePredictionFuture) | `structures` | [`Structure`](#openprotein.molecules.Structure), retaining all conformations |

A concrete task's bare reads select its primary output; requesting another named output preserves that output's decoded type. Ordinary `TaskFuture` uses the method default.

SVD, UMAP and GP are class-valued factories on `session.models`: fit a model, then call the fit future's `get()` or `wait()` to retrieve the fitted model. Use `get(output=...)` or `wait(output=...)` to read a named fit output. Use the fitted model's supported transform, prediction, chaining and deletion methods. Existing compatibility namespaces and typed job reload readers remain available. When the job record cannot distinguish its original specialization, GP fit, cross-validation, and prompt reloads retain their documented `PredictorModel`, `CVResultFuture`, and `Prompt` compatibility owners respectively; they do not promise the original exact subclass.

Fitted GP models expose their [trained kernel](/references/python-api/predictor#openprotein.predictor.TrainedKernel), prior mean and observation noise variance. The mean uses the trained property units; noise uses those units squared. Hyperparameters are unavailable for GPs trained before they were recorded. The compatibility predictor also does not expose them for ensembles.

Create embeddings for your protein sequences using open-source and proprietary models! Note that for PoET Models, you will also need to supply a [`Prompt`](#openprotein.prompt.Prompt).

sections.heading: Models
sections.prose: These embedding models inherit from a base [`EmbeddingModel`](#openprotein.embeddings.EmbeddingModel), due to their shared functionality in providing the [`embed`](#openprotein.embeddings.EmbeddingModel.embed) method. These can also be used to fit the [`Transform Models`](#transform-models).

sections.heading: Transform Models
sections.prose: These models are overlaid on top of the base embeddings models to produce reduced/transformed embeddings. [`SVDModel`](#openprotein.svd.SVDModel) represents an SVD model which is suitable to reduce the high-dimensional embeddings returned by base embedding models, whilst maintaining semantic information, fitted on your [`AssayDataset`](#openprotein.data.AssayDataset). You can fit your own SVD from any model's [`fit_svd`](#openprotein.embeddings.EmbeddingModel.fit_svd). [`UMAPModel`](#openprotein.umap.UMAPModel) represents a UMAP model which is suitable to project the high-dimensional embeddings into a lower dimension (usually 2) for visualization, to understand the semantic grouping within your [`AssayDataset`](#openprotein.data.AssayDataset). You can fit your own UMAP from any model's [`fit_umap`](#openprotein.embeddings.EmbeddingModel.fit_umap).
